a:r.a:t: REVISION NOTE: New opening. The old deck opened with logo animations and then a statistic. Judges remember stories better than numbers, so the pitch now opens on one concrete moment (a nurse, a sound, a lost recording) that the final slide resolves. It is labelled as an illustrative scenario: it describes how auscultation is documented today (concept note §II and §VI) and is not a claim about a real patient. If your team has a real story (a relative, a health worker you interviewed), swap it in. A true story is even stronger. SCRIPT (0:20): Tuesday, 9 a.m., a rural health unit in southern Palawan. A nurse hears crackles in a patient’s right lower lung. The doctor visits on Friday. [pause] By then, the sound is gone. All that’s left is a note: “crackles, right lower lobe.” Is the patient getting better or worse? No one can tell, because a stethoscope keeps nothing.
